text.tspan: Annual Report of the Great Lakes Regional Water Use Database Representing 2023 Water Use Data
By surface area, Lake Erie is the 12
lake in the world. The shallowest of the Great Lakes, it has
an average depth of 62 feet (19 meters) and a maximum
depth of 210 feet (64 meters). The lake holds about 116
cubic miles (483 cubic kilometers) of water. Lake Erie is
warmer than the other Great Lakes, which contributes to
its biological productivity. However, its small volume
relative to the other Great Lakes and overall average
shallow depth makes it more ecologically sensitive. The
watershed is home to more than 12 million people.
